ios-forms|Steppers.summary: Plenix on iOS sets how many of a product to buy with the system Stepper, as the web’s product options do with the quantity stepper: the count beside it in DM Mono, the stepper’s range from one to the stock or the limit per order, and its accessibility label naming the product. Apple’s default is a Stepper with its value in the label; Plenix keeps the Stepper’s taps, repeat and adjustable value and sets the count in the data font.

ios-forms|Segmented controls.summary: Plenix on iOS chooses a product’s size the way the web’s size buttons do: a segmented control when every size fits on one row and all are available, or a list of sizes with a checkmark when a size is out of stock and needs its note. The chosen size is said beside the option’s name (“Size: M”). Apple’s default segmented control has no disabled segment with a reason; Plenix keeps the control for short, available sets and moves to the list when a size needs words.

ios-navigation|Searching.summary: Plenix on iOS starts product discovery with the system search: a searchable navigation stack with suggestions from the catalog, the categories to browse while the field is empty, and the results as a grid of product cards with their prices in DM Mono. Apple’s default is a searchable list; Plenix keeps .searchable, its suggestions and its scope bar for the categories, and draws the results as Plenix product cards.
